title: A protocol for culturing _Drosophila melanogaster_ egg chambers for live imaging
protocol: Transfer 7-8 female flies of desired genotype and preferably 2-4 days old with a few males to a fresh food vial containing a small amount of fresh yeast paste.
Incubate at 25 °C for 16-18 hours.
Prepare Schneider's cocktail by supplementing Schneider's Insect Medium with 15-20% FBS and 0.6X Streptomycin/penicillin.
Adjust the pH to 7.00.
Store 10 ml aliquots at 4 °C for no longer than one week.
Use a fresh aliquot each day.
Immediately before use, supplement Schneider's cocktail with insulin to a final concentration of 0.2 mg/ml.
Anaesthetize 2-3 adult females of the appropriate genotype.
Fill a well of depression slide with Schneider’s medium cocktail containing insulin and place it under a dissecting microscope.
Keep a clean Lumox 50mm hydrophilic dish ready.
Gently grasp one pair of forceps to hold the female under the medium.
Use the other pair of forceps to pinch a bit of abdominal cuticle and pull, revealing the pair of white opaque ovaries.
Repeat this step for all the flies individually.
Collect the ovaries in the Schneider’s medium cocktail.
Hold the posterior part of the ovary with one pair of forceps where older egg chambers are located.
Hold the anterior tip of the ovary containing the germarium and very early stage egg chambers with another pair of forceps.
Very slowly pull the germarium or early stage egg chambers with the forceps at the anterior end of the ovary.
Carefully remove later stage egg chambers still attached to stage 8-9 egg chambers without touching mid-stage egg chambers.
Hold one end of older egg chambers with one pair of forceps and sever the connection between the stage 10 and older egg chamber with another pair of forceps.
Break a 22mmx22mm thin Fisher brand coverslip into two halves.
Place the two pieces approximately 1cm apart on the Lumox membrane.
Use a paintbrush to manipulate the pieces of the coverslip on the membrane.
Transfer egg chambers with approx. 45-50 μl Schneider's cocktail to the center of the dish between the coverslip pieces using a plastic transfer pipette.
Gently cover the egg chambers with a 22x22 mm cover slip.
Remove excess Schneider's cocktail gently from the sides of the coverslip until stage 10 egg chambers are completely immobile when shaking the Lumox Dish.
Surround the sides of the cover slip with a very thin layer of halocarbon oil 27 to minimize evaporation.
Mount the Lumox dish under the microscope for observation.
Identify an egg chamber of the desired developmental stage.
Adjust focus and exposure settings before starting time-lapse imaging.
Use heat suppression and neutral density filters to reduce tissue damage during long-term imaging.
Capture images at 20X magnification for up to 4-5 hours.
For spinning disc confocal imaging, use up to 63X magnification as needed.
Do not exceed 200 ms exposure time per frame for long-term movies.
Set intervals of 2 minutes between successive frames during time-lapse recording.
Refocus the sample between time-lapse images to account for movement in the z-axis.
Ensure egg chambers exhibit normal developmental processes such as border cell migration and oocyte growth.
Remove the cover slip from the Lumox dish slowly after the experiment.
Wash away the oil with ethyl alcohol.
Be cautious to avoid damaging the membrane of the Lumox dish from the sharp edges of the cover slip.
